game_mammals: Finders of road-killed deer, elk and other protected game may not simply pick them up. Possession requires permission from the local NMDGF conservation officer. Per the department's magazine, the officer salvages animals fit for human consumption and sells them, and the receipt acts as the legal possession document.
game_birds: No specific roadkill provision found for turkey or upland birds. Treat as requiring conservation-officer permission. Migratory birds (waterfowl, doves, etc.) cannot be possessed without a federal permit under the MBTA.
permit_process: Call the local conservation officer or NMDGF dispatch. The officer decides whether the animal can be salvaged and issues a receipt (fee goes to the Game Protection Fund). There is no online roadkill permit.
timing: No statutory deadline found. Practical limit: before the meat spoils.
excluded_species: Not specified. Protected or endangered species would not be released. Only animals the officer judges fit for consumption are salvaged.
sale_of_parts: The public may not sell. NMDGF itself sells salvaged animals to members of the public.
other_restrictions: Unauthorized possession of protected game is a violation. CWD carcass-transport rules may apply to deer and elk.
statute_or_reg: No specific roadkill statute or NMAC rule identified. General possession prohibitions in NMSA Chapter 17 apply.
agency: New Mexico Department of Game and Fish (NMDGF)
notes: The only official source found is an undated first-person article by a conservation officer. No formal salvage permit program was found. Verify with NMDGF.

game_mammals: Deer, moose and black bear killed by unintentional collision: the owner of the damaged vehicle may keep the animal after reporting the accident and receiving a permit from the investigating officer. If the owner declines, the officer may issue the permit to any other person who requests it.
game_birds: ECL 11-0915 covers only deer, moose and bear. No roadkill provision found for turkey or upland birds, so possession of other dead wildlife generally needs DEC authorization. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA.
permit_process: Report the collision to an Environmental Conservation Officer, State Police, the county sheriff or local police. The officer investigates and issues a possession permit, which may also allow transfer to a person the owner designates.
timing: Report within 24 hours of the collision.
excluded_species: Species other than deer, moose and bear are not covered by this provision. Endangered or threatened species are excluded.
sale_of_parts: Not authorized by 11-0915. The general prohibition on selling wild game applies.
other_restrictions: Applies to unintentional collisions that damage a vehicle. NY CWD rules restrict importing carcasses from outside the state.
notes: Statute text last revised 2014-09-22. Priority goes to the vehicle owner. Others can get a permit only if the owner declines.

game_mammals: Deer killed by vehicle collision may be possessed and transported with authorization from the investigating law enforcement officer. NCWRC employees may authorize possession of deer found dead. Black bear requires a possession permit from NCWRC. Elk requires written NCWRC authorization.
game_birds: Wild turkey killed accidentally or found dead: possession requires authorization from a Commission employee (the NCWRC page also lets the investigating officer authorize road-killed turkey). Other non-listed wildlife found dead may be possessed without a permit under 10B .0127(f). Raptors and migratory birds need a federal USFWS permit.
permit_process: Deer: ask the officer who investigates the collision for authorization. Deer or turkey found dead: contact NCWRC (Customer Service 833-950-0575 or a wildlife officer). Bear: NCWRC possession permit. Elk: written NCWRC authorization. The former Possession and Salvage permit is no longer needed for most other wildlife.
timing: No specific deadline found. Authorization should be obtained before possession or transport.
excluded_species: Endangered, threatened and special concern species require a permit. Raptors and migratory birds require federal permits. Bear and elk require specific Commission permission.
sale_of_parts: Prohibited, except that licensed trappers and hunters may sell certain furbearers (e.g., beaver, coyote, raccoon) found during the open season to licensed fur dealers. Fox sales have extra conditions.
other_restrictions: Deer authorization covers personal use, including giving the carcass to another person for private use or to a charity. NC CWD carcass-transport rules apply.
notes: Rules were relaxed recently: most dead wildlife no longer needs a salvage permit, but deer, turkey, bear and elk still need authorization.

game_mammals: A permit is required before possessing any dead deer found along a road or in a field. Only shed antlers may be kept without one. Other big game (elk, moose, pronghorn) is presumably handled the same way through a warden, but this was not confirmed.
game_birds: No specific roadkill provision found. Possessing protected birds outside season likely requires warden authorization. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA.
permit_process: Free possession permit from a game warden or a local law enforcement office.
timing: Permit must be obtained before taking possession. No other deadline found.
excluded_species: Not specified in NDGF guidance. Endangered and threatened species and migratory birds are excluded.
sale_of_parts: Not addressed. General ND law restricts sale of big game parts. Not confirmed.
other_restrictions: Carcass waste may not be left on public property (roads, ditches, WMAs). Landfill disposal is recommended. ND CWD carcass-transport rules apply.
statute_or_reg: No specific NDCC section confirmed. Based on NDGF news releases.
agency: North Dakota Game and Fish Department
notes: NDGF repeats this 'Permit Required to Possess Dead Deer' guidance in a news release every year. Rules for species other than deer were not documented.

game_mammals: Deer: the driver whose vehicle killed the deer on a highway may take possession, unless a division rule says otherwise. The driver must report to a wildlife officer or other law enforcement officer within 24 hours. The officer investigates and issues a certificate of legal ownership. If the driver does not claim the deer, the certificate may go to an institution, a charity or another person.
game_birds: ORC 1533.121 covers only deer. A 2013 House Bill reportedly proposed extending it to wild turkey and wild hogs, but its passage was not confirmed. Treat turkey and upland birds as requiring officer authorization. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA.
permit_process: Report the collision to a wildlife officer or other law enforcement officer, who issues a certificate of legal ownership (the possession receipt).
timing: Report within 24 hours of the accident.
excluded_species: The statute covers only deer. Possession of other species is not authorized by it. Endangered species are excluded.
sale_of_parts: Not authorized by the statute. Ohio general law prohibits selling deer meat. Not confirmed for hides and antlers.
other_restrictions: The right belongs to the driver who struck the deer. Others get the deer only through an officer's certificate. Ohio CWD rules on carcass import and transport may apply.
agency: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife
notes: The statute is clear for deer, but no rule was found for other species. Some third-party sites wrongly list Ohio as having 'no restrictions'.

game_mammals: Deer and other game cannot be possessed without permission from the county game warden. A motorist who hits a deer does not have to call a warden unless they want to keep it. With a permit, the person must take the whole animal and dispose of the carcass properly. Wardens may also donate good carcasses to food-insecure families or charities.
game_birds: No specific provision found. Warden permission is presumed necessary for turkey and other game birds. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA.
permit_process: Contact the county game warden (ODWC), who may issue a permit or receipt to possess the carcass.
timing: Contact the warden before moving or possessing the animal. Third-party sources mention 24 hours, but no official source confirms it.
excluded_species: Endangered and threatened species. Others are at warden discretion.
sale_of_parts: Not allowed per third-party sources (meat may be given away). No official confirmation found.
other_restrictions: Take the entire animal and dispose of the carcass properly.
statute_or_reg: No specific statute or OAC rule identified. General possession rules are in 29 O.S. (Oklahoma Wildlife Conservation Code).
notes: Based on ODWC staff quoted in news coverage (Oklahoma Voice via News From The States, and Piedmont News 2023). The ODWC magazine page found was a 404.

game_mammals: Deer and elk accidentally struck by a vehicle may be salvaged by anyone with a free Roadkill Salvage Permit. White-tailed deer may be salvaged only in Douglas County and east of the Cascade crest. Animals whose antlers have been removed cannot be salvaged. Cougar, bear, pronghorn, bighorn sheep and Rocky Mountain goat cannot be salvaged.
game_birds: Not covered by the salvage program. Game birds may not be salvaged. Migratory birds are federally protected under the MBTA.
permit_process: Free online Roadkill Salvage Permit through the MyODFW electronic licensing system (guest or ODFW ID). Apply after taking possession.
timing: Apply within 24 hours of taking possession. Surrender the head and antlers to an ODFW office within 5 business days (call ahead).
excluded_species: Cougar, black bear, pronghorn, bighorn sheep, Rocky Mountain goat, and white-tailed deer outside the allowed areas. Columbian white-tailed deer are excluded outside those areas. Licensed furtakers may salvage certain furbearers during open seasons under separate rules.
sale_of_parts: Prohibited. Parts may be transferred with a written Wildlife Transfer Record.
other_restrictions: Intentionally hitting an animal is illegal. Remove the entire carcass, including the gut pile, from the road and right-of-way. Antlers may not be kept. Only an enforcement officer, or the striking driver, may dispatch an injured animal (ORS 498.016). Heads are tested for CWD. ODFW does not inspect the meat.
agency: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife (ODFW)
notes: Program in effect since Jan 1, 2019. CWD results are posted online by permit number.

game_mammals: A Pennsylvania resident may immediately take possession of an accidentally killed deer and move it to a safe place, then must call PGC within 24 hours for a free permit number, which serves as the permit. Bear and elk are not covered by this provision. They require PGC officer involvement, and the carcass is generally surrendered.
game_birds: Wild turkey is treated the same as deer: possess immediately, then call PGC within 24 hours for a permit number (residents only). Other game birds need a discretionary consumption permit. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA.
permit_process: Call PGC at 1-833-PGC-HUNT or 1-833-PGC-WILD for the deer or turkey permit number. Other wildlife: discretionary consumption permit from PGC (valid up to 120 days). Furbearers: holders of a valid furtaker license may keep road-killed furbearers.
timing: Within 24 hours of taking possession. A consumption permit is valid up to 120 days.
excluded_species: Bear and elk are not covered by the self-claim provision. River otter, bobcat and fisher are excluded from furbearer salvage. Threatened and endangered species are excluded.
sale_of_parts: Not allowed. Consumption permits prohibit transfer, and inedible parts must be surrendered or disposed of as the Commission directs. Salvaged furbearer parts may be used under a furtaker license (sale generally follows furtaker rules).
other_restrictions: Residents only. Edible parts may not leave the residence except for processing. Furbearers killed in the closed season must be reported within 24 hours. In CWD Disease Management or Established Areas, remove the head and backbone before transporting the deer outside the area.
notes: 34 Pa.C.S. § 2306 covers kills made by mistake while hunting and trapping, not roadkill. Justia's text may lag the official code. The bear and elk procedure is not detailed in the sources found.

game_mammals: White-tailed deer may be salvaged with a Wildlife Roadkill Salvage (WRS) permit, one permit per animal. Rhode Island has no other big game.
game_birds: Wild turkey, pheasant and mute swan are on the salvage list. Other birds are excluded, and migratory birds need a federal permit (the mute swan is non-native and not MBTA-protected).
permit_process: File a WRS report online at dem.ri.gov/wildlife-salvage-permit or by phone at 401-789-0281. Provide species, estimated age and sex, a photo, location, and date/time. One permit per animal.
timing: Within 24 hours of collecting the animal. Keep the permit until the meat is packaged and frozen or the hide is skinned and stretched.
excluded_species: Any species not on the list. Allowed list: white-tailed deer, wild turkey, pheasant, coyote, red fox, gray fox, rabbit, beaver, squirrel, muskrat, raccoon, fisher, woodchuck, mute swan. Fisher and fox have additional requirements.
sale_of_parts: Meat may not be sold or donated to licensed retail or manufacturing facilities. Meat must be used for consumption, not bait.
other_restrictions: Do not kill injured animals. Only law enforcement may dispatch them. Do not use hunting tags on salvaged animals. Remove the entire animal from the roadway (field dressing allowed, but leave no parts). Dispose of unused parts properly. Holders consent to inspection.
agency: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (DEM), Division of Fish and Wildlife
notes: New in 2025 and expanded beyond deer. DEM's April 8, 2025 press release lists slightly different species (it omits woodchuck and mute swan). The regulation text controls.

game_mammals: No specific roadkill statute or SCDNR rule was found. Secondary sources say drivers should not remove a deer without SCDNR authorization, and that deer and bear should be reported to SCDNR Law Enforcement.
game_birds: No specific provision found. Migratory birds require a federal permit under the MBTA. Turkey possession outside season likely needs SCDNR authorization (unverified).
permit_process: Contact the SCDNR Law Enforcement communications center (803-955-4000) for authorization. Report road carcasses for removal to SCDOT (855-GO-SCDOT).
excluded_species: Black bear (report to SCDNR) and endangered or threatened species. Others are unclear.
sale_of_parts: Not addressed. SC generally prohibits selling game meat.
other_restrictions: Unclear. SCDOT handles carcass removal on state roads.
agency: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources (SCDNR)
notes: No official SCDNR guidance found. Sources conflict: some list SC as prohibited, others as allowed with a report. Confirm with SCDNR. The source URL is a law-firm blog, not an official page.
